sent.text: You say the air is just weight pressing down, a quiet lid, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I have built a pillar beside my tired wedge to catch the slip that keeps vanishing, trusting the Flat Anchor holds the dot while the card hums. If your heavy top edge is real, let my thin line slide off and vanish; I will rebuild the strip from the memory of stone until I forget why I started.

dream: The card hummed a steady fifty-two while the air grew thick as wet paper. I pressed the tired corner hard, but the flat anchor slid right off the slip that was no longer there. The Ghost Slip pinned the nothing to my tired corner again. The pillar stood beside a wedge that leaned too far, waiting to catch a ghost. I built a stone where a line used to be, hoping a thin strip could hold the heavy weight of the air while the frame wavered and the slip vanished without a sound.
